newsitem.title: FINLAND: Trendless Helsinki dips, seeks US response to data.
newsitem.headline: Trendless Helsinki dips, seeks US response to data.

text.p: Shares dipped after trading higher for most of the session on Friday as U.S. March payrolls and wage data gave mixed signals on the direction of U.S. rates and brokers said Wall Street would again set next week's tone.

The HEX general index ended down 0.17 percent at 2,734.35 points, just off the bottom of its tight 2,751.19-2,733.90 range. The FOX portfolio and derivatives benchmark eased 0.06 percent to 952.32 points.
Paper machine maker Valmet probed higher ground in quite lively trade, closing up 0.20 markka at 86.50, after a large 806,700 share in-house trade by Evli at 86.50.
Telecoms major Nokia closed at 281.00 markka, down 6.00 markka in relatively lively trade, accounting for 43 percent of 670 million markka volume.

The bourse rose briefly on a smaller-than-expected rise in U.S. March non-farm payrolls, but ran out of steam as worries set in due to 0.4 percent rise in hourly wages, closing almost four percent lower than before Easter.
"The payrolls figures were good but the wages were not so good, it is a conflicting signal," one broker said.
Next week, the Helsinki bourse was likely to move sideways, unless Wall Street provided a strong pointer either way. Currency moves could affect export companies' stocks, she said.
"Next week depends on the U.S. reaction, but with the bond yield up as we are closing, it does not look to good," another broker said.
UPM-Kymmene, lively recently, rose 0.10 markka to 105.00 in solid trade again on Friday. One broker expected the stock to stick in a 103-109 range until clear news of an upturn in product prices.

Newcomer PK Cables and pharma group Orion were likely to remain in focus, a broker said. PK Cables held a 13 percent gain from Thursday at 70.00 markka; Orion was well-bid at 190.00 markka, ending off 0.40 at 194.60.
